summary: The S&P 500 index added 0.23% to close at 7,670.18, reversing yesterday's modest decline as the defensive rotation that dominated Monday unwound and technology reclaimed leadership, with the Nasdaq 100 gaining 0.62% while the Dow essentially went nowhere at +0.04% to 53,438.42. The 10 year yield fell further to 4.64%, down 1.25%, and TLT gained 0.95% to 83.35 as oil dropped 3.07% to 82.40 on signals that the US is pursuing economic rather than military pressure on Iran, removing the inflation fear that had weighed on bonds the prior two sessions. Gold extended its rally to 4,697.50, up 1.22%, and Bitcoin touched above 81,000 intraday before settling at 79,420.35, up 0.58%, with the debasement trade clearly back in style as concerns over Bessent's bond buyback program and a 40 trillion dollar debt pile keep hard assets bid. Consumer confidence came in at 90.3 against a forecast of 100.0, the lowest reading in seven months, with gas prices above 4 dollars per gallon cited as a primary drag, a softer number than markets feared but still a deteriorating signal. Canada announced retaliatory tariffs on approximately 20 billion dollars of US goods after trade talks collapsed, and KOSPI fell 3.12% in Seoul, the worst global performer of the session, suggesting the trade war is registering real damage in export dependent economies. The market's undivided attention now shifts to NVIDIA's earnings report Wednesday, Core PCE and preliminary GDP also Wednesday, and Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech Friday.
